result:
Both integrate one branch's changes into another; difference is history shape. `git merge` joins the two histories with a new merge commit (two parents) → existing commits untouched, true record of when branches diverged and joined, but graph gets noisy. `git rebase` replays your commits one by one on top of the target → linear history, no merge commit, but every replayed commit gets a new SHA (history rewritten).

Consequences: rebase on commits already pushed and shared → others' history diverges, needs force-push (`--force-with-lease`), so only rebase local/private branches. Conflicts: merge resolves once; rebase may ask per replayed commit. Undo: merge is one commit to revert; rebase recovery goes through `git reflog`.

Verdict: rebase to tidy your own feature branch onto latest `main` before sharing; merge to bring shared branches together.
